title: Construction of Modular Hydrogel Sheets for Micropatterned Macro-scaled 3D Cellular Architecture
protocol: Produce micro-scale patterns using SU-8 photoresist on a silicon wafer via photolithography.
Weigh out 12.5 g of PDMS and 2.5 g of curing agent solution with a ratio of 1:5.
Mix the PDMS and curing agent thoroughly.
Degas the mixed PDMS in a vacuum chamber to remove bubbles.
Spread the degassed PDMS evenly onto a micropatterned silicon wafer within a foil casting dish.
Place the silicon wafer on a heated plate at 65 °C for 90 min to cure the PDMS.
Remove the cured PDMS from the casting dish and silicon wafer.
Cut the edges of the cured PDMS.
Place the cut PDMS onto a petri dish with micropatterned side up.
Wash the PDMS mold using 70% ethanol for primary sterilization.
Rinse the PDMS mold with distilled water.
Dry the PDMS mold completely in an oven at 65 °C for 10 min.
Dissolve and mix 3 g of a powdered nonionic surfactant in 100 ml of distilled water to create a 3% (w/v) coating solution.
Place the micropatterned PDMS molds in a plasma cleaner and clean them for 1 min at 85 W, 0.73 mbar.
Coat the surface of the PDMS with the surfactant solution for at least 3 hr using a laboratory rocker.
Wash the surfactant solution from the PDMS molds.
Dry the molds completely in an oven at 65 °C for 10 min.
Sterilize each micropatterned mold by exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation over 30 min.
Dissolve 0.1 g of sodium alginate powder in 10 ml of phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate and mix the solution overnight to dissolve the powder completely.
Filter the solution through a 0.22 μm filter connected to a 1 ml syringe.

Culture HepG2 cells in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium (DMEM) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin until 70% - 80% confluence in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Wash the cells once using PBS.
Add 1 ml of 0.05% trypsin-EDTA for 4 min to trypsinize the cells in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the cells harvested from the culture dish at 250 x g for 3 min.
Resuspend the cells using 1 ml of PBS following removal of the supernatant.
Count the number of single distributed cells in PBS using an automated cell counter.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 250 x g for 3 min.
Remove PBS from the centrifuged cell pellet.
Add 1 ml of a 1% (w/v) sodium alginate solution to the remaining cell pellet.
Mix the cell and sodium alginate gently using pipetting.
Incubate the cell/hydrogel suspension in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Dissolve 1.47 g of calcium chloride dehydrate in 100 ml of ddH2O to produce a cross-linking reagent (i.e., 100 mM CaCl2·2H2O).
Rinse the interior of a humidifier with ultrasonic transducer using 70% ethanol.
Fill the humidifier with 200 ml of the cross-linking reagent.
Clean micropatterned PDMS molds in a plasma cleaner for 1 min at 85 W.
Load 7.2 μl of well-mixed cell/hydrogel suspension at the edge of the micropattern in the mold.
Turn on the humidifier to produce a mist of the cross-linking reagent.
Spray the cross-linking reagent onto the hydrogel precursor for 5 min, covering the topographic surface within a range of 5 cm.
Detach each hardened hydrogel sheet from the micropatterned molds via pipetting PBS gently around the hydrogel sheet using a 200 μl pipette tip.
Pick up each floating hydrogel sheet using an end-cut 1,000 μl pipette tip end.
Transfer a single layer of the hydrogel sheet into 1 ml of DMEM in a 12-well plate.
Culture cells in vitro in a floating manner using the hydrogel construct as a unit component in the 12-well plate over a week in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Exchange the culture medium every other day.
Sterilize the PDMS frame and nylon filter papers in an autoclave for 15 min at 121 °C.
Place the sterilized PDMS frame onto a quarter of a piece of nylon filter paper in a petri dish.
Transfer a modular hydrogel sheet into the interior of the PDMS frame using a pipette tip.
Align the edge of each modular hydrogel sheet with the PDMS frame using an empty pipette tip.
Repeat steps to form a stack of 4 - 6 layers.
Remove the culture medium by flowing it out through the pillar structures at the bottom of the PDMS frame.
Add 2 µl of alginate solution (2% w/v) at a corner of the multi-layer construct.
Spray a mist of the cross-linking reagent for 30 sec onto the multi-layer construct.
Use 2 ml of mist of the cross-linking reagent (at a spraying rate of 250 ml/hr).
Rinse the multi-layered construct gently with 400 µl DMEM.
Remove the PDMS frame using tweezers.
Detach the multi-layered construct from the filter paper by gently wiping with a cell lifter following the addition of 4 ml of DMEM.
Transfer the multi-layered construct to a 6-well plate containing 3 ml of DMEM using filter paper.
Culture the cells in vitro in a floating manner with the hydrogel construct as a multi-scale cellular scaffold in the 6-well plate over a week in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Exchange the culture medium every other day.
